item.title: AI and the future of shopping: are we ready for what’s coming?
item.description: On this episode of America First , Scottie Nell Hughes looks at the new trend of surveillance shopping. AI can now predict when and where we plan to spend our hard-earned bucks. Stores can take that information and change prices on an hourly basis to maximize profit. But is this an unfair strategy, one that is harmful to the consumer? And is it even legal? Or is this a future inevitability that we all have to accept? Joining Scottie for this conversation are Dr. Tamara Patzer, author and creator at the Daily Success Media Network, and Michael Wynne, an attorney who focuses on US federal criminal investigations and trials.

item.title: The impact of the World Cup: Can it help heal a war torn world?
item.description: On this episode of America First , Scottie Nell Hughes reflects on the legacy of the World Cup. The recent North American tournament was a grand success. Nations from all over the world found a chance to interact and unite under the umbrella of association football. But is the World Cup a blip on the radar in a world experiencing more and more conflict, or can it make a more significant impact on bringing nations together? Scottie examines these questions with guests Angie Wong, Republican Committeewoman for Miami-Dade County, and Armen Kudrian who is running for Congress in California. Don’t miss it.

item.title: Looking for justice: The unexplained case of Seth Rich
item.description: On this episode of America First , Scottie Nell Hughes re-opens the file on the case of Seth Rich. Mr. Rich was a young Democratic staffer, who was found murdered on the streets of Washington DC a decade ago. Since his death, rumors have been swirling about an odd connection to the DNC. Scottie explores the latest with attorney and investigative litigator Ty Clevenger.

item.title: The GOP is looking to win the midterms
item.description: On this episode of America First , Scottie Nell Hughes discusses the recent RNC midterm convention. Usually conventions are only held in presidential election years. But this time Trump and MAGA are looking to reinvigorate the party as it stares down the barrel of the gun of Democrats flipping both the House and Senate. Can the GOP parry the blow and keep at least the Senate and maybe both chambers, or will the legislative branch be stripped from the president’s grasp? Joining Scottie for this discussion are conservative pundit Steve Malzberg and the host of the Mike Schwartz show, Mike Schwartz.

item.title: Dying off: Can congressional term limits save the American republic?
item.description: On this episode of America First , Scottie Nell Hughes examines the average and growing age of American politicians. Recent examples of politicians withering into old age while in office include Dianne Feinstein, Joe Biden, and Mitch McConnell. So, should the US enact term limits at the federal and state levels? Or would this lead to the few actually competent leaders we have being run out of office before their time? Joining the conversation are John Pudner, President of Freedom and Family Action, and Carson Carpenter, host of The Common Cause.

item.title: Flock cameras and the rise of mass surveillance
item.description: On this episode of America First , Scottie Nell Hughes takes a look at the world of mass surveillance. Over the past five years so-called flock safety cameras have spread across the United States. They are meant to read car license plate numbers and their manufacturers say they are purely for safety and assisting law enforcement. But that has not stopped citizens from being concerned about surveillance. Some have even taken it into their own hands and begun destroying flock cameras. Scottie is joined by Justin Robert, a freedom advocate, and Maria Zeee, host at Zeee Media.
